title: A Minimum-Cardinality Genuinely Unextendible Product Basis in Three Qutrits
authors: Fei Shi, Ge Bai, Xiande Zhang, Qi Zhao, Lvzhou Li
abstract: It has remained an open question whether a genuinely unextendible product basis (GUPB) exists. We resolve this problem by constructing an explicit three-qutrit GUPB of cardinality fourteen in the smallest tripartite Hilbert space in which a GUPB can exist. Together with the nonexistence of three-qutrit GUPBs of cardinality less than fourteen, our construction proves that fourteen is the minimum cardinality. A padding procedure further extends the construction to all tripartite systems whose local dimensions are at least three. As applications, the normalized projector onto the thirteen-dimensional orthogonal complement of the three-qutrit GUPB is positive under partial transposition and bound entangled across every bipartition, while the GUPB exhibits strong quantum nonlocality without entanglement.
summary: This paper resolves the open problem regarding the minimum size of a Genuinely Unextendible Product Basis (GUPB) in three-qutrit systems. The authors construct an explicit basis of cardinality 14, proving this is the minimum possible size for this system. They also demonstrate that the associated projector exhibits strong quantum nonlocality while remaining bound entangled across all bipartitions.
main_problem: The authors addressed the open question of determining the minimum cardinality required for a Genuinely Unextendible Product Basis (GUPB) in tripartite quantum systems.
main_result: They constructed an explicit three-qutrit GUPB with a minimum cardinality of fourteen, proving this is the smallest possible size for such a basis in this setting.
method: The proof combines graph theory analysis (using orthogonality graphs) with rigorous mathematical constructions and computer-assisted searches to establish both existence and minimality bounds.
model_or_system: The study focuses on three-qutrit systems ($\mathbb{C}^3 \otimes \mathbb{C}^3 \otimes \mathbb{C}^3$) in quantum information theory, generalizing the results to arbitrary local dimensions $d_A, d_B, d_C$.
key_observables: The constructed basis exhibits 'strong quantum nonlocality without entanglement,' and the projector onto its orthogonal complement is shown to be positive under partial transposition (PPT) and bound entangled across every bipartition.
important_parameters: Minimum cardinality = 14 for the three-qutrit case; local dimensions $d \ge 3$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on Lemma 1, which provides necessary and sufficient conditions relating the UPB property to rank conditions on local vector subsets.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the local orthogonality graphs ($G_A, G_B, G_C$) whose union covers $K_{14}$, while Tables I-IV detail the specific vectors, determinant certificates, and index sets used in the construction and verification process.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem definition (GUPB), uses graph theory to constrain possible bases, constructs the explicit basis of size 14 for three qutrits, proves its minimality, generalizes the construction to higher dimensions, and finally analyzes the entanglement properties of the orthogonal complement.
why_interesting: The concept of GUPBs is central to understanding quantum nonlocality and separability criteria. Demonstrating a concrete example that exhibits strong nonlocality without violating PPT conditions provides deep insight into multipartite quantum correlations beyond simple entanglement measures.
